goal: Review the native Windows metadata inspector patch for LAB-01A.
scope: Experimental fix/lab-01a-win-native-preflight branch at base 8d99d57e09e82f5d25b55885383a0eff6a6cb0dd. Code changes are limited to the canonical preflight inspector and its Python tests. Local review only; no publication or signed AA execution grant.
plan: Review the full code and documentation diff against the recorded base SHA.
Confirm native metadata behavior in an authorized Windows QA context, including real junctions if that context permits them.
Resolve or explicitly retain blocked coverage and obtain human review before any PR preparation.
risks: Windows enumeration metadata and no-follow stat reduce exposure but do not prove that every cloud provider exposes every placeholder state or remove filesystem races.
Python 3.11 compatibility is based on API selection and synthetic tests; it was not executed under Python 3.11.
Two real-link Python tests remain skipped on the current host; the synthetic junction fixtures are not real Windows junction integration.
The general suite remains unaccepted and two process-terminating suites remain blocked by policy.
The synthetic Windows metadata fixtures use native path rules of the test host; they do not establish full Windows path semantics on Linux.
R4.1 separates host-independent Windows path policy tests from Windows filesystem metadata fixtures; no Linux or macOS execution of this candidate is claimed.
Real junctions, case-sensitive NTFS boundaries and filesystem races remain unverified.

incidents.symptom: Synthetic Windows fixture read native st_file_attributes eagerly even when a flag override existed.
incidents.provenance: Operator reported Linux AttributeError; runtime R3 RED reproduced AttributeError using a stat object with only st_mode.
incidents.cause: flags.get(path, original.st_file_attributes) evaluates its default argument before lookup; root fallback and tag constants also depended on host metadata.
incidents.resolution: Fixtures now supply synthetic Windows attributes and tags for entries and root, and patch tag constants only within the simulated context.
incidents.verification: R3 GREEN on Windows Python 3.12; Linux runtime execution NOT_RUN.
incidents.residualRisk: Synthetic sys.platform does not emulate Linux or Windows path semantics across hosts.
incidents.nextAction: Run the Python tests on a real authorized Linux host before cross-platform acceptance.

incidents.symptom: An external link elsewhere in the tree left dependencyState missing and freeBytes zero despite local node_modules.
incidents.provenance: R2 code inspection shows the final classification guard; R3 RED junction fixture failed while resolving ordinary node_modules; original real-link test was SKIP on this host.
incidents.cause: Final dependency and disk classification was gated on absence of externalLinks, datalessFiles and metadata errors.
incidents.resolution: Classify node_modules during safe entry inspection and calculate disk capacity after root verification, independently of unrelated unsafe entries.
incidents.verification: R3 GREEN targeted synthetic external-link and offline-placeholder cases; unsafe entries still block the preflight exit.
incidents.residualRisk: Real symlink and junction integration remains unverified; races remain possible.
incidents.nextAction: Review the candidate and run real-link tests only in an authorized capable environment.

incidents.symptom: A legitimate Windows junction may be reported outside the workspace when os.readlink returns an extended-path prefix.
incidents.provenance: External reviewer path comparison; R4 local synthetic Windows junction fixture reproduced application-level false external classification.
incidents.cause: Extended drive spelling and normal drive spelling were compared as different anchors.
incidents.resolution: Normalize only recognized extended drive and extended UNC link text to their ordinary Win32 forms; reject device, drive-relative and ambiguous spellings.
incidents.verification: R4 RED extended internal target classified external; GREEN internal target accepted, external extended target blocked, unknown namespaces rejected. Synthetic Python 3.12 Windows; native junction integration NOT_RUN.
incidents.residualRisk: UNC behavior has synthetic external classification only; no real junction or remote share integration. Filesystem races remain.
incidents.nextAction: Human review of bounded support and native integration gap before commit decision.

incidents.symptom: Case-sensitive NTFS directory boundaries and dependency names may be classified incorrectly by case-insensitive Path equality.
incidents.provenance: External reviewer reported metadataComplete true, dependencyState local and empty externalLinks; R4 reproduced a case-changed workspace boundary; R4.1 RED reproduced NODE_MODULES falsely classified local.
incidents.cause: Path membership, enumeration and dependency equality previously used case-insensitive matching without verified identity.
incidents.resolution: Require exact workspace component spelling and exact enumerated names; classify node_modules only by exact child name; reject case-colliding directory enumeration.
incidents.verification: R4 and R4.1 RED/GREEN synthetic Windows fixtures; R4.1 20 PASS, 2 SKIP on Windows Python 3.12.10. Native case-sensitive NTFS integration NOT_RUN.
incidents.residualRisk: Cannot certify all native case-sensitive NTFS or concurrent mutation behavior without authorized native integration; conservative false rejection is possible.
incidents.nextAction: Human review of bounded guarantee and native integration gap before commit decision.

incidents.symptom: Windows fixtures inferred Windows path behavior from POSIX tempfile paths and host os.path.normcase when only sys.platform was patched.
incidents.provenance: Independent reviewer report supplied by operator for Linux Python 3.13.5; local code review confirmed host-dependent fixture semantics. No Linux execution of R4.1 by local runtime.
incidents.cause: Patching sys.platform does not change pathlib or os.path host path rules.
incidents.resolution: Extract pure Windows link parsing and exact membership into PureWindowsPath/ntpath helpers with host-independent lexical tests. Native enumeration fixtures explicitly skip on non-Windows hosts with separate pure coverage; use ntpath.normcase for Windows collision detection.
incidents.verification: R4.1 Windows Python 3.12.10: 22 total, 20 PASS, 2 SKIP. Pure lexical tests cover drive, extended drive, relative, UNC, extended UNC, case boundaries and rejected namespaces. Linux/macOS NOT_RUN.
incidents.residualRisk: Native enumeration and real case-sensitive NTFS behavior remain Windows-only and unverified on a case-sensitive volume; no cross-host runtime PASS is claimed.
incidents.nextAction: Review test split and run the portable lexical suite on an authorized Linux host if cross-host acceptance is required.
